metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40.00), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon following such events.
- Mean reversion is strong in 7–14 day window; if forecast exceeds 50% of 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–15% for next 5–10 days.
- Sentiment history is flat (0.00) in all examples — no behavioral signal — so do not adjust for sentiment unless sentiment > 0.30 or < -0.30.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop >10% from prior day, model often fails to recognize — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon following such drops.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence — cap maximum forecast at 5% above 30-day moving average unless event-driven (e.g., policy change, auction).
- If true outcome shows persistent low values (e.g., <35.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to ignore — apply downward bias for next 5–7 days, especially if no event context.
- No event context provided — no adjustment for external shocks; rely solely on price history and sentiment (which is neutral).
